entities.title: The sim in Rust, the picture in Godot 4
entities.summary: A pure, deterministic Rust sim at 12 Hz with no engine dependency, presented by Godot 4 through godot-rust.
entities.context: The mechanics must stay retro and provable by replay while the art is modern.
entities.decision: lodestar-core holds the rules with no Godot dependency; lodestar-bridge and lodestar-godot present it through gdext; scenes and scripts are GDScript.
entities.rationale: Rust for the rules, Godot for the picture; the same crates run headless in tests, in parity replays and later in a server.

entities.title: Desktop only
entities.summary: Windows, macOS and Linux; the web build is out of scope.
entities.context: godot-rust in Godot's web export is still experimental.
entities.decision: Native desktop exports only; keyboard and mouse.
entities.rationale: Desktop removes the sign-in gate, file-size limits and browser-owned keys.

entities.title: Hybrid: one sim for single-player and a later server
entities.summary: Single-player embeds the sim; a later multiplayer server runs the same crate as the authority.
entities.context: Multiplayer may come later and must not drift from the client's rules.
entities.decision: Nothing in the single-player design may assume the sim lives in the same process as the picture: the presentation reads snapshots and events only.
entities.rationale: One set of rules, so a server never drifts from the client.

entities.title: Source layered after the diagrams essay
entities.summary: Use cases → features → capabilities in Rust, with infrastructure, presentation and hosting around them, and .dev views beside the code.
entities.context: Agents find their way by the folders.
entities.decision: The layout of DESIGN § Project layout, enforced by the crate graph and tests/layers.rs.
entities.rationale: The diagrams stay true and the dependencies point inward.

entities.title: You always see your ship
entities.summary: An EVE-style orbit camera, space-anchored by default, zoom 1.5× to 5× the ship's length.
entities.context: The original shows the view from the cockpit; LodeStar's art shows the ship.
entities.decision: The one deliberate change to how the game plays; the four mounts stay and the pilot picks the active one.
entities.rationale: The owner's choice; the rules and scanner stay as they are and play-testing decides any retune.

entities.title: Clean-room roles
entities.summary: Implementers read only docs/ and the documents beside the code; only the spec-and-verify role reads the baseline.
entities.context: The repository is public and the remake must not copy the original or the private faithful clone.
entities.decision: RULES is written from the baseline in LodeStar's own words; the code is written from RULES; parity is proven with data-swapped traces.
entities.rationale: Nothing of the original's data or expression enters the repository.
